section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: In natural first-language acquisition, the four language skills — Listening, Speaking, Reading, Writing (LSRW) — typically develop in which order?

options.option_text: Listening → Speaking → Reading → Writing
Writing → Reading → Speaking → Listening
Reading → Writing → Listening → Speaking
All four develop simultaneously with no order

explanation: A child first listens and absorbs language, then speaks; reading and writing are literacy skills learned later, typically in school. This natural order informs the direct/structural approaches to language teaching.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: The Structural Approach to teaching English emphasises:

options.option_text: Teaching sentence patterns and structures through graded, controlled practice
Teaching only isolated vocabulary lists with no sentence context
Complete avoidance of grammar in any form
Teaching literature analysis exclusively, before any grammar

explanation: The Structural Approach (associated with Palmer, Hornby) teaches language via graded sentence patterns/structures with controlled, repeated practice — building competence systematically rather than isolated word lists or pure literary analysis.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: A teacher has pupils role-play ordering food at a restaurant, focusing on getting the message across rather than perfect grammar. This reflects:

options.option_text: Communicative Language Teaching (CLT)
Grammar-Translation Method
Rote memorisation of grammar rules
Silent reading with no speaking practice

explanation: CLT prioritises real-life communicative competence and meaningful language use (like role-play) over strict grammatical accuracy — the opposite emphasis of the Grammar-Translation Method, which centres on rule memorisation and literal translation.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: The Bilingual Method of teaching English, proposed by C.J. Dodson, uses the mother tongue mainly to:

options.option_text: Give quick, accurate meanings of new English words/sentences before English-only practice
Completely replace English instruction with mother-tongue lessons
Teach only translation exercises with no spoken practice
Discourage any use of English in the classroom

explanation: The Bilingual Method uses brief mother-tongue equivalents to clarify meaning quickly, followed by extensive practice in English itself — a middle path between pure Direct Method (English-only) and Grammar-Translation (heavy reliance on translation).

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: A teacher explains new English words using objects, actions and pictures in the classroom, avoiding the mother tongue entirely. This is the:

options.option_text: Direct Method
Grammar-Translation Method
Bilingual Method
Translation-only Method

explanation: The Direct Method teaches entirely through the target language itself — using realia, gestures and context rather than translation — building an intuitive feel for English, unlike Grammar-Translation which relies heavily on the mother tongue.
